title: Audrey Werro runs 800m meet record in Lausanne Diamond League win, Femke Broeders-Bol lowers Dutch national record
content:
Audrey Werro won the women’s 800m on home soil at the Lausanne Diamond League, holding off Femke Broeders-Bol to win with a meet record time of 1:55.33s.

It was a patient race from Werro, 22, who last week won the European crown by beating Keely Hodgkinson of Great Britain and Dutchwoman Broeders-Bol. Here, on home soil, the Swiss athlete ran from the front, as pacemaker Myrte van der Schoot went out a little fast, splitting 54.64s through halfway — well under world-record pace.

Werro surged smartly at 500m to cover a move by world champion Lillian Odira, 18, and had enough of a gap on the field in the home straight to win by eight hundredths. Broeders-Bol closed hard in second place, showing immense speed endurance to lower her own national record to 1:55.41s and jump three places on the all-time list to 18th.

Odira, the silver medallist at the Commonwealth Games this July, faded in the home straight from fourth to seventh. Ethiopia’s Saida Tsehaye produced a personal best of 1:56.92s for third.

This is a significant win for Werro, her ninth outdoor victory from 10 races this summer, with the odd one out being the European Championship semi-final, when she tripped with 150m to go and was advanced to the final.

“I really enjoyed the race, the turnaround after the European Championships was very short, so I had to recover quickly, and I felt more tired than usual today,” she told Diamond League media.

The Swiss athlete has put together one of the greatest seasons in women’s 800m running. Here, she took down Hodgkinson’s meet record, running 0.33s quicker than the Briton did this time last year. This is the fifth time in 2026 that Werro has broken 1:56, including her 1:53.80s clocking at the Stockholm Diamond League, when she beat Hodgkinson for the first time and became the quickest 800m runner since Jarmila Kratochvilova set the world record in 1983.

Only Pamela Jemilo (eight times in 2008) and Caster Semenya (five times in 2018) have ran sub-1:56 more times in one season than Werro, with the Swiss athlete scheduled to race against Hodgkinson and Broeders-Bol on home soil (again) next week, in Zurich. The trio should meet again in September at the inaugural World Ultimate Championships.

Meanwhile Broeders-Bol, in her debut season after moving up from the 400m hurdles, continues to improve. “The European (Championships) gave me confidence, and this race gives me even more confidence that I belong with the best,” she told Diamond League media. “I need to trust myself, keep pushing after 500 metres, stop protecting myself too much and simply enjoy racing.”

Elsewhere in Lausanne, Marco Arop’s frontrunning tactics backfired in the men’s 800m. The Canadian went through halfway in 48.86s, behind pacemaker Patryk Sieradzki, leading a field which included Olympic and world champion Emmanuel Wanyonyi, and Olympic bronze medallist Djamel Sedjati.

Wanyonyi of Kenya won in 1:42.19s, a little more than a second slower than his lifetime best, run on this track in 2024 after his Olympic success. Algeria’s Sedjati was the runner-up (1:42.31s) and U.S athlete Brandon Miller overtook Arop, running 1:42.55s to leave the Canadian fourth.

Incredibly, it’s a first 800m Diamond League win of the season for Wanyonyi, 22, who had raced this distance three times without victory — notably beaten by American teenager Cooper Lutkenhaus in Oslo — though did set a 1,000m world record in Monaco this July.

“It didn’t go very well,” Arop told Diamond League media, now down 14-6 in the head-to-head against Wanyonyi. “I wasn’t feeling so good after the warm-up, but I wanted to push the pace. Maybe it wasn’t the smartest move, but when I say I’m going to go for it, I go for it.”

Sprint hurdler Masai Russell recorded her 10th win from 11 races in 2026. She won the 100m hurdles in 12.27s, a meeting record and the sixth time this season that she has broken 12.3 seconds. Nadine Visser, the Dutch woman who took a long-awaited European gold at last week’s championships, was second in 12.42s, seven hundredths ahead of third-place Alaysha Johnson.

On Thursday night at the street meet held beside Lake Geneva, Sweden’s Mondo Duplantis won the men’s pole vault with a 6.21m clearance, five days after claiming another European title. He was pushed all the way by Greek vaulter Emannouil Karalis, who cleared 6.16m at the second time of asking, just one centimetre off his lifetime best.

Duplantis, the world-record holder at 6.31m, did have two failed attempts at 6.32m before retiring, having jumped more than he normally needs to for the win. Karalis’ mark is the best ever by a runner-up — 10cm more than the previous highest non-winning jump.
